articles.title: Chat mode: tell Shokker what you want
articles.summary: CHAT opens a studio with the helper on the left and a live preview on the right. Say what you want in plain words and the car changes, with Undo for every step; see what it can and cannot do (it cannot open, save or export).
articles.what: Chat is the easy front door to the same booth. It works on the same paint, zones and spec as PRO, so nothing is a second copy. The helper on the left builds on what is on the car, and the car on the right updates as it goes. Tabs show the Paint, the Shine (spec) or the Car parts Shokker knows. A view strip under the car mirrors the Full Editor views, and a layer bar on the right lets you lock the helper to one layer. Every step is saved under Versions, and Compare slides between before and after. It works with no key at all: the built-in helper has a guided builder, a design library of more than 70 themes, and Surprise me. An AI key or Claude through MCP adds free-form chat.
when: You would rather describe the look than set sliders.
You want four quick design ideas to react to.
You are editing a finished livery ("make the black matte").
how: Load your template or paint, then click CHAT in the mode switch (or the AI button, bottom right).
Type what you want, for example "make the hood matte black", "retro red white and blue stripes", or "numbers gold chrome", and press Enter.
Look at the preview. Press Undo under that answer if it is not right, or Another take for a different idea.
Press Surprise me for four complete ideas tried on your car, or Colours from a picture to design in a logo's colours.
Press Render & save when you like it, or Full editor to continue in PRO.

faq.q: Is Chat a different program from PRO?
faq.a: No. It edits the same paint, zones and spec. Full editor takes you back to PRO.

faq.q: Do I need an AI key?
faq.a: No. The guided builder, the 70-plus themes and Surprise me work free.

faq.q: Will Chat change my numbers?
faq.a: Not unless you name them.

faq.q: How do I go back a step?
faq.a: Press Undo under the answer, say "undo", or click an earlier step in Versions.

faq.q: Can Chat save my paint?
faq.a: No. Press Render & save, or use PRO.

faq.q: Can the AI helper do the setup for me, or do I have to build every zone by hand?
faq.a: The helper can do it: in Chat describe what you want in plain words and it builds the zones, finishes and colours for you, with Undo for every step. You can still fine-tune any zone by hand in PRO; both edit the same car.

articles.title: Offline helper, AI key or Claude: what each does
articles.summary: Offline Helper answers app questions from local knowledge and can turn supported colour, material and Zone requests into plans. Read the proposed target and operation before choosing an action. It is not ChatGPT or Claude, and it cannot promise a new custom drawing or discover exact car panels from a general car name. Choose Claude or ChatGPT/Codex for a connected conversation using your own account and the setup card. A factual question here gives advice; it does not approve a paint change.

faq.q: Are you ChatGPT? Which model are you?
faq.a: Offline Helper is local Shokker software. Claude or ChatGPT/Codex takes part only when you choose that provider and connect a listening conversation.

faq.q: Is typing what I want enough for the AI helper?
faq.a: Yes. In chat mode describe what you want in plain words (make the hood red) and the helper shows how it read it and changes the car when you press Run, with Undo.

faq.q: Does typing a numeric spec request into Offline Helper guarantee that exact channel value?
faq.a: No. The reviewed current numeric shorthand converts supported numbers to approximate named looks such as gloss, satin, matte, metallic or chrome; it is not an exact raw-channel setter. Inspect the proposed finish and composed spec before applying. Before applying anything, verify that the proposed action matches your request; asking about a number does not authorize a paint change.

faq.q: How does Offline Helper interpret roughness50 compared with g50?
faq.a: The reviewed numeric shorthand uses different internal scales: letter g50 is divided by255, while roughness50 is divided by100. It then picks an approximate named look; this does not write the exact green byte50. Treat this as a current limitation, check the proposed finish, and keep raw-channel values separate from strength percentages.

articles.title: Changing what is already on the car
articles.summary: Most people start from a finished livery. Tell Shokker "make the black matte" or "numbers purple metallic" and it finds that colour on the car and changes only that.
articles.what: Shokker reads the real colours in your paint (not the template's dead space), so "the black", "all the red" or "the dark blue" point at pixels that are actually there. It then changes only those: a look alone (matte, satin, chrome, powder coat, wet look) changes the shine and keeps your colour; a new colour repaints exactly those pixels; both together do both. Words such as "a bit glossier" or "darker" are understood too. If you name a colour that is not on the car (say pink when the car has red), it asks rather than guessing. A second request on the same colour edits the zone it made, so changes stack instead of resetting. Numbers, sponsors and logos are changed only when you name them.
when: You loaded a finished paint and want to change one colour or a look.
You want a matte or satin version of a livery.
You want numbers or stripes a different colour.
how: Load the finished paint (PSD with layers is best, or a flat TGA).
In Chat type for example "make the black matte", "numbers purple and metallic", "everything that is white, make it satin", or "powder coat the yellow".
Check how it read the request in the builder, then press Run.
Not right? Press Undo under that answer. Say "a bit more" or "do the same for the roof" to keep going.
tips: A look word alone (matte, satin, chrome) keeps your colours exactly; it changes only the shine. Add a colour word to change the colour too.
Say "except the numbers" or "but leave the numbers alone" to protect them.
pitfalls: On a flat paint (no layers), numbers, sponsors and stripes are not known; Shokker asks you to show them first.
"Red matte" may include a dark-red tail-light lens because it matches by colour.

faq.q: Does "make it matte" change my colours?
faq.a: No. A look word alone changes only the shine.

faq.q: Why did "red matte" touch my tail-light lens?
faq.a: It matches by colour, so a dark-red lens can be included. Undo and name the part.

faq.q: Does it work on a flat TGA?
faq.a: Yes, but a layered PSD is best. On a flat paint it asks you to show numbers, sponsors and stripes.

faq.q: How do I protect the numbers?
faq.a: Say "except the numbers" or "leave the numbers alone".

faq.q: How do I recolour only the red parts to blue?
faq.a: In Chat type "make the red blue": Shokker finds the real red pixels on the car and repaints only those. By hand in PRO, pick the red as a zone: + Add Zone, PICK COLOR FROM CAR and click the red, raise the tolerance if edges are left over, then set BASE > Base Color to Use solid color and choose blue. Check the preview and press Undo if it caught too much, such as a dark-red lens.

faq.q: Can I change one colour on a paint I already have?
faq.a: Yes. Tell the helper the colour and what you want ("make the black matte", "the white satin"). It picks that colour on the car as a zone, so only those pixels change and the rest stays. If the colour is not on the car it asks instead of guessing.

mistakes.symptom: A colour you named is not changing
mistakes.cause: That colour is not actually on the car, or is a different shade
mistakes.fix: Answer the helper's question to point it at the right colour.

mistakes.symptom: Numbers changed along with everything else
mistakes.cause: You named a colour the numbers also use
mistakes.fix: Undo and add "except the numbers".

protips: For best results load the layered PSD. Layers let the helper tell stripes, numbers and sponsors apart, which a flat TGA cannot.

articles.title: Picking colours and looks in plain words
articles.summary: Chat understands everyday colour words, hex codes, parts, "the black on the hood", slang like "powder coat", and even "same shade as the hood".
articles.what: You do not need a painter's vocabulary. The helper reads colour words (including shades such as powder blue or charcoal), hex codes, and phrases such as "all the red", "the dark blue" or "the black on the hood". It maps spoken looks to real catalogue finishes: powder coat, plasti dip, cerakote, matte, satin, gloss, wet look, chrome, satin chrome, dark chrome, metallic, pearl, candy and more. Compound sentences ("make the hood and the roof powder coat, then the stripes gold") are split into steps. If a word is ambiguous it asks with buttons instead of guessing.
when: You are not sure how to name a colour or a look.
You want to be precise about which part or colour changes.
how: Type the request in plain words, or use a hex code like #ff7eb6.
To match a colour on your car say "same shade as the hood".
Name a part or a colour on the car: "the roof", "all the red", "the black on the hood".
Answer any question it asks by clicking a button.
tips: Add a look and a colour in one go: "matte metallic purple on the left side".
"A bit glossier" or "darker" nudges what is there rather than replacing it.
pitfalls: Colour names are read by family; "pink" on a car with only red will be asked about, not forced.
Spelling mistakes in common words are understood, but made-up looks are asked about.

deep.heading: Colour families

articles.title: The AI gear: key, model and daily cap
articles.summary: In the Chat gear you paste an OpenRouter key and use one model (DeepSeek v4.1 Flash is recommended). A daily spending cap stops runaway costs.
articles.what: The gear (cog) in the AI panel is where you add an online key. Paste your OpenRouter key and press Save; it is stored on this computer, encrypted for your Windows account. The Model line shows the one model the helper will use. DeepSeek v4.1 Flash is recommended: it is the cheapest that works well, around half a cent per request. If you pick a different model the gear warns that it usually costs more and offers Use the recommended model. The Daily cap (default $2 per day) is checked before every request, and Test connection and Check credit are there too. The When switch chooses Auto (AI only when the built-in helper is not sure), Always, or Off. A private option runs a model on your own PC through Ollama or LM Studio. A key is optional.

The helper says the daily cap has been reached.

Get a key at openrouter.ai/keys, add a few dollars of credit, and paste it in the Key line. Press Save.
Leave the Model on the recommended one.
Set the Daily cap you are comfortable with, and keep When on Auto.
Press Test connection to check it.

articles.summary: Yes. Choose Claude in the AI panel and follow the Claude Desktop or Claude Code setup card. It uses your own Claude account; an installed connector still needs a connected, listening conversation. ChatGPT/Codex has its own setup choice in the same panel.

articles.title: How the helper learns your car
articles.summary: Known cars are recognised from the sheet layout and the car folder. A car that is new to Shokker is taught once, remembered on your computer, and confirmed before use.
articles.what: The helper climbs a ladder when you ask for "the hood". First it looks for a match in the shipped car library, by sheet layout or iRacing car folder. If the sheet is at least 78% like a known car, it proposes that car's layout fitted to your sheet and waits for one click; it never applies a look-alike silently. If nothing is close, it shows your sheet and asks you to draw each part. Everything you confirm or teach is stored on this computer and recognised next time, including other paints of the same car. If your paint has lost its template dead space, the helper can still recognise many cars from where panel edges fall, but treats that as a proposal to confirm.

articles.title: The AI helper cannot download a template or any file from the internet
articles.summary: The AI helper, offline or online, never downloads anything from the web: no template, PSD, logo or picture. You get the file yourself and open it with Open Paint..., or you show the helper the car parts.
articles.what: Asking the AI to find, fetch, grab or download a template, a PSD, a logo or a picture from the internet changes nothing: it cannot browse, cannot open a link and has no download step, so nothing is downloaded and nothing on your car changes. This holds for the offline helper and for Claude or ChatGPT working through the connector, because the Shokker tools they use only act on what is open in the app. What works is a short hand-off. You download the paint template for your exact car yourself, from iRacing or a trusted source such as Trading Paints or your league, open it in Shokker with Open Paint..., and then the helper does the paint job on it. The car library already knows 31 checked iRacing templates, and for any other car you show the parts once and the helper remembers them.
when: You asked the AI to download or find the car template and nothing happened.
You want to know whether the helper can fetch a file, a logo or a picture from the web.
You are not sure how to get the template into Shokker.
how: 1. Download the paint template for your exact car yourself, from iRacing or a trusted source such as Trading Paints or your league.
2. In Shokker press Open Paint... next to Source Paint and pick the file: Layered template for a PSD, Flat image for a picture.
3. Set the iRacing Car Folder to your car's paint folder (the Browse button next to the box).
4. Ask the helper for the paint job. If the car is not in the car library it asks you once to show the parts (teach parts) and remembers them.
5. For a logo or picture: save it to your computer, then drop it on the Sponsor Kit box (Car menu) or add it as a layer.
tips: Once the template is open, the helper can place, size, recolour and finish everything on it in words.
You can also describe the look you want in words and the helper builds it from the Shokker catalogue without any download.
pitfalls: Do not send the helper a web link and expect it to open: it will not.
Use the template made for the SAME car you drive; every car has its own sheet layout.

deep.heading: What the helper can reach
deep.body: Only what is open in Shokker and the files you give it. It reads your zones, layers and preview, knows the whole finish catalogue and can aim at named parts of the car. It has no browser, no download step and no way to open a link.

deep.heading: The two-step hand-off
deep.body: First you get the template: download it from iRacing or a trusted source, then open it with Open Paint.... Second the helper takes over: ask for the paint job in words and it applies it to the open template. If the car is new to it, show the parts once.

faq.q: Can the AI just download the template for me?
faq.a: No. The helper does not download files from the internet. Download the template yourself from iRacing or Trading Paints and open it with Open Paint....

faq.q: Can the helper find my car template on the internet?
faq.a: No, it cannot browse or open links. Use the car library, show it the parts, or open the template you downloaded.

faq.q: Can Claude or ChatGPT fetch a file for me through the connector?
faq.a: No. The Shokker tools they use only act on what is open in the app. They have no download step.

faq.q: If the AI cannot download it, where does the template come from?
faq.a: You get it yourself, from iRacing or a trusted source such as Trading Paints or your league. Then Open Paint... next to Source Paint.

faq.q: Can the AI go online and look up the template of a car?
faq.a: No. It cannot browse or search the web. It knows the 31 checked templates in the car library and learns any other car from the parts you show it.

faq.q: Can the helper download a logo or a picture?
faq.a: No. Save the file to your computer, then drop it on the Sponsor Kit box or add it as a layer.

faq.q: Does the helper know my car without a template?
faq.a: It knows 31 checked iRacing templates in the car library. For any other car you show the parts once and it remembers them.
